text:
Qiao: Heads-up — need a quick decision on span naming for LLM requests before we wire the new OTLP exporter. Want something consistent for dashboards + low-cardinality for exporters. Quick takes?
Riley: +1 on consistent. My proposal: keep span.name generic like `llm.request` and push model/variant/tokens/cache as attributes. Example: `span.name = \"llm.request\"`
Riley: attrs -> `llm.model: gptx-13b`, `llm.model.family: gptx`, `llm.model.variant: int8-q4`, `llm.tokens.input`, `llm.tokens.output`, `llm.kv_cache.hit` (bool), `routing.policy: low-latency|cost-optimized`, `quota.tier`. Don’t bake token counts into span.name.
Max: Strong +1. Also: token counts explode cardinality if raw. Suggest token bucketing attr: `llm.tokens.bucket = \"0-128\"|\"128-512\"|...\"` so dashboards can group without high cardinality.
Lina: Privacy check — we cannot put prompt text or customer identifiers in spans; make sure `user.*` is redacted. Also avoid any full prompt hashes in attributes unless approved. We can keep `request.size_estimate` instead of actual prompt size if needed.
Qiao: Good call. What about model-family in the span name for easier filtering? e.g. `llm.request.gptx` vs plain `llm.request`?
Riley: That helps humans but creates many distinct names over time. Prefer `llm.request` + `llm.model.family` attribute. UI can show `llm.model.family` as a primary column. Keeps trace index small. :thinking:
Max: For KV cache hits we should emit both: attribute `llm.kv_cache.hit=true` on the span and a metric `llm.kv_cache.hit.count` (counter) tagged by model.family + routing.policy. Metrics are cheaper for long-term retention & aggregation.
telemetry-bot: OTLP exporter connected to tracing-prod namespace. Default sampling: adaptive tail-sampling 1%.
Lina: Sampling note — make sure token-heavy requests get a higher sample rate (we can boost sampling for `llm.tokens.bucket=\"512-2048\"` or for errors). Also don't export full token counts to low-retention backends.
Qiao: OK we need a short RFC: required attributes for spans and recommended retention/sampling. Propose: spans TTL = 14d, long tails for sampled failures = 90d, metrics retention = 365d, token histogram aggregates = 365d but raw token counts in spans only kept for 14d.
Riley: That matches my thoughts. I'll draft RFC with canonical attribute list + example OTEL resource mapping and exporter config. Quick example for the RFC snippet:
```
span.name: "llm.request"
attributes:
  llm.model: "gptx-13b"
  llm.model.family: "gptx"
  llm.model.variant: "int8-q4"
  llm.tokens.bucket: "128-512"
  llm.kv_cache.hit: false
  routing.policy: "low-latency"
  quota.tier: "enterprise"
```
Riley: Will open PR in `infra/telemetry/trace-schema` and tag you all. @channel if anyone absolutely needs a different shape speak now.
Max: One tiny addition — normalise model names before emitting (lowercase, replace `/` with `-`, strip commit hashes). Saves a lot of dashboard noise.
Lina: Also add `llm.model.quantization` and `llm.model.sequence_limit` attributes so we can correlate latency regressions without joining raw logs.
Qiao: Perfect. If there’s no blocker I want us to land default span schema by EOD so dedicated exporter work can proceed.
Riley: Roger. Draft coming in ~30m.
